title: Untangle presubmit origami and introduce release-handshake
author: Priya Menon
description: Context: The presubmit pipeline has accreted a tangled set of concerns: language-aware lint runners, telemetry shims, toolcache priming, and a fragile release hook. This PR decomposes the presubmit 'origami' (folded biz-logic inside the monolithic runner) into composable adapters and adds a deterministic 'release-handshake'—a lightweight protocol between presubmit and the release orchestrator to reduce flakey merges during release windows. Motivation: Reduce presubmit maintenance surface, speed up fastpath green merges, and provide a visible, auditable gate for release merges. Design summary: 1) Split presubmit into three adapters: lint-adapter (language plugins), toolcache-adapter (lazy priming and cache hints), telemetry-adapter (uniform metrics and provenance stamps). 2) Introduce release-handshake: a small state machine and annotated commit-status that the release orchestrator listens to; presubmit will mark candidates as READY_FOR_RELEASE only when the selected smoke-suites pass and release-prober acknowledged. 3) Add an opt-in fallback that allows non-release branches to follow previous fastpath behavior. Checklist: - [x] extract lint plugin registry and wire to adapter interface; - [x] implement toolcache hint emitter and lazy priming flag; - [x] introduce telemetry envelope (trace-id + presubmit-phase) and route to ci-metrics; - [x] implement release-handshake state transitions and annotated status context; - [x] add unit tests for adapter plumbing and handshake FSM; - [x] update docs (CONTRIBUTING.md presubmit section) and release runbook; - [x] coordinate with Release team for rollout. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on presubmit (flag off by default), enable in Canary repos for 48h, switch to broad rollout when handshake has 12h of stable traffic. Related: ENG-3120 for presubmit rearchitecture; ENG-3199 for release reliability.
